ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Consolidated Canadian Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, the Unite Nations Act list, the Criminal Code money-laundering offence benchmark, and, due to US Dollar payment rails, the OFAC SDN list and UN Consolidated List. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are defined under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations; enhanced due diligence is required for all domestic and foreign PEPs, family members, and close associates. FINTRAC Risk-Based Approach guidance is applied to all KYC/CDD documentation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada NUANS Name Search (Online Filing Centre, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Federal corporate names may be in English, French, or both official languages. Non-Latin script names require an English or French transliteration/transcription compatible with the NUANS phonetic system. The name must be distinctive, not confusing, and comply with the Canada Business Corporations Act and Canada Business Corporations Regulations, 2001; a bilingual form may be required to carry on business in Quebec.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any word implying Crown patronage, a regulated profession, or a business requiring a statutory licence
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, the applicant must, within 60 days of the rejection notice, submit a written reconsideration request to the Director, Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada, together with the original NUANS report and a legal memorandum demonstrating that the name is distinctive and clearly not confusing. The Director will issue a written decision. A subsequent judicial review may be brought before the Federal Court under section 246 of the Canada Business Corporations Act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or registered-agents address with a street address (not a post-office box) is permissible for the registered office under section 19 of the Canada Business Corporations Act. However, the registered office cannot serve as the actual resin manufacturing or storage site; a separate physical production and inventory address must be identified for municipal zoning, health, and product-safety compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of 15% likelihood of an unannounced municipal by-law or CRA GST/HST site visit within the first three years; low sector-specific risk because the business is non-financial and classified as Standard Risk under FINTRAC AML/CFT risk tiering.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA), R.S.C., 1985, c. C-44; ss. 5-14 (incorporation), ss. 49-50 (share capital), ss. 102, 106 and 114-116 (directors, officers and indemnification), ss. 119-120 (registered office and records), s. 233 (annual return).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 4001) filed online through the Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; no escrow account requirement. Federal CBCA corporations may be capitalized with common shares issued for cash or property at director-fixed consideration; share proceeds are not blocked or escrowed at formation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accepts the initial subscription for common shares, fixes the issuance price per share, and authorizes issuance upon receipt of funds. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [address] in [province], where the corporate records will be maintained. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed President, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. RESOLVED, that the proposed bylaws are approved and officers may take all steps necessary to comply with the CBCA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: NUANS Name Search and Reservation (or Numbered Company Election)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre / NUANS search house via ISED
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Order a current NUANS name search report for the proposed corporate name, verify the name is distinguishable from existing federal and provincial names, and, if desired, file the report together with Articles of Incorporation. If no name is required, elect to incorporate as a numbered company on the online form.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report dated within 90 days
Consent of any person whose name is used
Proposed corporate name and legal element (Inc./Corp./Ltd.)
Registrant and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusion or prohibited character, choose a new name and obtain a fresh NUANS report, or proceed as a numbered company by amending the incorporation request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Articles of Incorporation: set out corporate name or numbered company, registered office address in a Canadian province, authorized share classes and any share restrictions, first directors (at least 25% resident Canadians where required), and any business restrictions. Submit and pay the federal filing fee via credit card; the Certificate of Incorporation is issued electronically.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 4001 - Articles of Incorporation
NUANS name search report (if named corporation)
Names and residential addresses of initial directors
Direction for registered office address and jurisdiction
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Corporations Canada sends a deficiency notice, correct the stated defect and re-submit within the response window; if the name is rejected, re-file using a numbered company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting and Appointment of Officers/Registered Office Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial board of directors under CBCA; internal corporate records at registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold an organizational meeting of the initial directors (may be by unanimous written consent). Adopt the bylaws, confirm the registered office as the legal seat for service, appoint the corporate officers, approve the issuance of initial shares, and execute share certificates. Keep the minute book, share register, and corporate seal (if adopted) at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Bylaws of the corporation
Minutes/consent resolution of initial directors
Share subscription and share certificates
Officer appointment resolutions and acceptance of office
Minute book, share register, and corporate seal (if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any failure to hold a formal meeting is cured by executing a directors' written resolution circulated for unanimous consent and, where applicable, a waiver of formal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, create the corporation's CRA Business Number using BRO. Register the federal corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and payroll deductions account if applicable. These registrations are immediate and linked to the corporate BN, which is also required for opening bank accounts and applying for permits.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
CRA Business Registration form (RC1) or BRO data
Names and Social Insurance Numbers of responsible officers
Corporate registered office and mailing address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or queries the registration, verify the legal name and business number; submit a corrected registration through CRA Business Account or call the CRA Business Enquiries line.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada (annual return) and provincial/municipal licensing desk where operations are conditioned
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File any required annual return under CBCA s. 233 at the anniversary date; update Corporations Canada within 15 days of any change in registered office or directors. Comply with federal and provincial filing obligations before activating manufacturing operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
CBCA annual return form (at anniversary)
Notice of change (if directors/registered office changed)
Any provincial business licence documents (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Consequences for late annual return: make the filing online immediately, pay the late filing fee, and, if struck off, apply for reinstatement with payment of arrears.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing authority applies to ISIC 3240 polyresin statue manufacturing under federal law; general municipal business licensing and provincial workplace safety rules may apply at the physical facility location.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No special federal or provincial operating licence is mandatory for hand-painted polyresin statue production; a general municipal business licence and building/occupancy permit may be required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / provincial environmental ministry (if triggered)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full federal Impact Assessment Act screening for small-batch resin statue casting; provincial environmental registration/approval may be required only if VOC or waste thresholds are exceeded.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions from resin and paint solvents must meet local and provincial air quality limits; wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer-use bylaws; hazardous waste must be segregated, stored in approved containers, and disposed of by licensed waste transporters under provincial hazardous waste regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If the corporation operates a physical workshop: obtain fire code inspection/certificate and building occupancy permit; secure structural load clearance for storage racks and equipment; implement WHMIS, SDS, ventilation, and emergency exit procedures; register with the provincial workers' compensation board and carry required occupational injury insurance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); online portal: CRA My Business Account (GST/HST, payroll, corporate income tax) and the Canada Business Number (BN) registration portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada or earning Canadian-source income must register for a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN) via the CRA's 'Register a Business Number' online service or by completing Form RC1. For GST/HST purposes, the entity must open a separate GST/HST account under the same BN and file Form RC1A (Request for GST/HST Account Information). A foreign entity without a Canadian permanent establishment may register on a voluntary basis to claim input tax credits and to zero-rate exported goods and services; the BN/GST/HST account is obtained online using the entity's legal name, registered office address, and evidence of foreign incorporation. Non-resident registrants must designate a resident agent or representative for service of process and CRA correspondence where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box regime under the Income Tax Act. A corporation incorporated in Canada is a taxpayer in its own right and is subject to federal Part I corporate income tax, with provincial income tax allocated by permanent establishment. Non-resident corporations are taxable under Part I on Canadian-source business income and on certain capital gains; no statutory election is available to treat a corporation as a partnership or disregarded entity for federal income tax purposes. For GST/HST purposes, a non-resident may elect to have a related 'qualifying registration' shared GST/HST group (section 150 of the Excise Tax Act) to streamline compliance. Canadian-resident partnerships and joint ventures holding the corporation's shares may be eligible for the 'look-through' or 'fiscally transparent' rules that are available in the applicable provinces, but these do not alter federal corporate classification. Hybrid mismatch rules under subsection 18.4(8) and section 247 of the Income Tax Act restrict deduction effectiveness for 'hybrid instrument' arrangements and for payments made to fiscally transparent foreign entities where the payee jurisdiction does not tax the income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: PHP 0 (non-resident supplier making taxable supplies in Canada through a permanent establishment must register; elective registration permitted; no federal threshold applies to a non-resident with a physical presence, although the CRA generally applies the 30,000 CAD 'small supplier' threshold to residents; non-resident vendors of goods to Canadian customers may be required to register under the 2019 GST/HST framework for 'digital economy' supplies if their global revenues exceed CAD 30,000 and Canadian-source taxable supplies generate more than CAD 30,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system. The CRA requires that all GST/HST registrants issue, retain, and produce on request invoices that satisfy the requirements of section 169 of the Excise Tax Act: the supplier's name and BN, the date of issue, the recipient's name (or nominee), the total taxable amount, the rate, and the amount of tax charged (expressed separately). E-invoices in PDF or structured electronic format (XML, EDI, or API-transmitted) are accepted; a machine-readable summary must be archived for six years. There is no pre-clearance from the CRA before issuing an invoice; the CRA performs post-transaction verification through data matching. Registrants must file GST/HST returns electronically when their revenues exceed CAD 1.5 million, or by paper where lower. Real-time clearance, customs coding, or fiscal stamp obligations do not exist at the federal level.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A zero-rated supply of goods for GST/HST purposes includes a supply of tangible personal property (including resin statues and garage kits) that is exported from Canada by the supplier or by the recipient, as described in section 1 of Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act. The supplier must have documentary proof that the goods were exported within the required 60-day period (or longer for goods on consignment or in bond). For services provided to non-residents relating to the goods (e.g., design, prototyping, or custom molding of the resin statue), zero-rating applies under section 7 of Part V of Schedule VI only if the recipient is outside Canada and the service is not for consumption in Canada. The entity must maintain an export trail showing ownership of the goods did not pass in Canada and that the goods left Canada in an unaltered state from the point of export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B3 or CAED/CUSMA when applicable),
Commercial Invoice with Incoterms and stated export sale
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank wire/payment proof from the foreign buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA may deny a zero-rating benefit where the exporter fails to produce the documentary evidence within the prescribed timeframe. The penalty for knowingly making a false statement or omission on an application for a rebate or refund is CAD 100 per false statement, plus an additional penalty equal to 50% of the amount of the rebate or refund claimed (Election, subparagraph 280(1)(c)(ii) and subsection 285(1)). Where a zero-rating is applied to a supply that did not in fact leave Canada, the CRA may assess the GST/HST due (5% or HST where applicable) on the full selling price, charge interest, and impose penalties under amended subsection 280(1.1). Fraudulent claims also expose the exporter to criminal prosecution under section 327 of the Excise Tax Act and severe monetary penalties of up to CAD 100,000 or imprisonment of up to 5 years for answerable offences. Additionally, where a rebate of input tax credits has been claimed in respect of a zero-rated export and the goods are subsequently returned into Canada, a GST/HST assessment will be raised on the value of the returned goods unless the exporter takes steps to re-export them, and export eligibility may be clawed back for a 12-month period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); Canada has no separate foreign-exchange administration. Exchange and monetary policy functions are carried out by the Bank of Canada, the Department of Finance, and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), with anti-money-laundering and cross-border transaction oversight by FINTRAC.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible under a free-floating regime. Current account and capital account transactions are generally unrestricted; there is no exchange control law requiring official authorization for dividend remittances, interest, royalties, or branch profits. Non-resident direct investment into a Canadian Business Corporation is lawful, and funds may be repatriated freely in CAD or foreign currency. The principal remittance hurdles are tax compliance rather than currency controls: Part XIII withholding tax on dividends/interest/royalties, transfer pricing documentation under sections 247 of the Income Tax Act, and adequate solvency and board authorization under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA). A resident Canadian director requirement under the CBCA and CBSA customs valuation reporting apply, but there is no convertibility restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, no mandatory conversion timeline, and no minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in an authorized foreign-currency bank account. Exchange control reporting does not arise; however, Statistics Canada balance-of-payments surveys and FINTRAC large electronic funds transfer reporting may require the bank to report a cross-border transaction of CAD 10,000 or more, and export documentation must support the commercial purpose.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW-to-MEDIUM viability as a primary liquidity rail. Canada does not issue an electronic money institution licence; foreign digital EMI platforms (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) may be used as secondary payment collection or vendor-payment gateways, but they are not CDIC-insured banks and cannot provide a full Canadian clearing account. A foreign EMI that services Canadian customers must register as a money services business (MSB) with FINTRAC and comply with PCMLTFA. For the resin statue preorder and garage-kit trade model, the primary operating and clearing account must be maintained at a Schedule I Canadian bank; EMIs should be used only to optimize settlement of small cross-border merchant receipts and supplier disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The CBCA requires at least one director to be a resident Canadian, or, if fewer than four directors, at least one director must be a resident Canadian. Most Schedule I banks permit remote onboarding for a corporation where the resident Canadian director and beneficial owner can be verified by video and digital identity proofing under PCMLTFA. Physical presence at a branch is generally mandatory for non-resident directors, sole non-resident UBOs, or where the company is unable to provide reliable independent source-of-funds documentation. For a CA_CORP with a non-resident beneficial owner, the account-opening protocol may require an in-person KYC interview for the non-resident director OR a face-to-face meeting with an authorized signatory who is a resident Canadian, supported by the full corporate bundle and a certified copy of the CBCA certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregated preorder deposits received through Stripe and PayPal with no customer-level wire details, creating a mismatch between the bank statement descriptor and underlying commercial receivables.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform merchant agreements; daily settlement reports from Stripe/PayPal; order-level invoice logs; customer preorder confirmations; refund and chargeback exception reports; CRM reconciliation proving each deposit corresponds to a valid resin statue preorder; and a notarized certificate of beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large one-time inbound equity injection from a foreign parent or related holding company in a low-tax jurisdiction, where the source of funds and economic substance of the shareholder are difficult to verify.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry extracts for every entity in the ownership chain; CBCA/articles of incorporation and by-laws; board resolution authorizing share subscription and capital contribution; shareholder registry; source-of-funds statement supported by audited financial statements; group organizational chart; bank reference letters from the originating bank; and a completed FINTRAC/MSB beneficial-ownership declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound trade payments to resin casting suppliers, tooling workshops, and raw-material vendors in jurisdictions with elevated sanctions or trade-control risk, particularly China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, or Vietnam.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial invoice; purchase order; underlying supply contract; packing list; bill of lading/airway bill; customs entry record (including HS code 3240 or NAICS 339930 mapping); bank confirmation from the receiving bank; know-your-supplier questionnaire; sanctions screening results; and a statement of end-use and ISIC classification affirming no restricted military or counterfeit use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the registered office address of CA_CORP, the director residential addresses, and the location of bank transaction activity, especially if registered office is a corporate agent and directors are non-resident.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Status from Corporations Canada; registered-office agent agreement; proof of physical operating location (lease or utility bill); certified director identity documents and proof of residential address; explanation of the corporate agent/P.O. Box arrangement; and personal income or residency verification for each director or UBO.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocols: inbound equity capital from a foreign parent should be wired by SWIFT MT103 to the CA_CORP operating account at a Schedule I bank, with the beneficiary account name exactly matching the registered corporate name. The wire remittance information (Field 70) must state 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SHARE SUBSCRIPTION / CA_CORP' and, if using ISO 20022 payment messages (pacs.009 or pacs.008), the purpose code should be mapped as 'EQUI' or the bank-approved 'capital transfer' purpose. Verification must include a board resolution approving the share subscription, a subscription agreement, updated share register, source-of-funds declaration, organizational chart, and a certificate of good standing for the parent. The bank will perform FINTRAC large EFT reporting if the transaction equals or exceeds CAD 10,000; funds settle through Lynx (formerly LVTS) for CAD or over the SWIFT gpi or CHIPS network for USD. Any inward direct-investment transaction must be captured in the company's internal balance-of-payments reporting and should be matched to the subsequent issuance of shares in the Canadian corporation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The preferred clearing rails for trade settlements are SWIFT MT103 for direct open-account supplier payments and commercial documentary letters of credit issued by the Canadian bank for larger tooling and production batches. For MT103 wires, payment instructions must include the supplier's full legal name, bank account, IBAN or domestic account number, SWIFT/BIC, and the resin statue or garage-kit invoice reference. CAD payments clear through Lynx, USD through CHIPS/Correspondent banking, and CNY through an offshore CNH clearing bank or CIPS participant where available. For commercial L/Cs, the terms must comply with UCP600 and include a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or air waybill, insurance certificate, and optionally a pre-shipment inspection certificate. Standby L/Cs may be used as performance guarantees for the Asian manufacturing subcontractors, but routine preorder deposits and small ticket settlements should use MT103 to minimize bank fees and documentary discrepancies.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts and CAD/CNY outright forwards, with tenors from spot to 24 months, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and CSA, provided the notional does not exceed forecast commercial exposures.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on CNY/USD and TWD/USD or other restricted currencies, cash-settled in CAD or USD, allowed only where the underlying exposure is a confirmed purchase order, supplier invoice, or binding trade contract.

Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD/CNY) for matching equity-capital injections, intercompany loan servicing, and long-term working-capital repayment streams, subject to OSFI derivatives prudential expectations and internal counterparty credit limits.
Plain-vanilla FX options, zero-premium collars, and participating forwards to hedge the timing risk of preorder conversion cycles and seasonal raw-material purchases.

NDF rollovers, CME-listed CAD/USD and CNY futures for margin-managed treasury liquidity, and dual-currency deposits with simultaneous forward/option overlays, all restricted to documented trade hedges and prohibited from speculative trading under the treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under s.133, Canada Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary of incorporation each year; due date recurs annually on the same calendar rule (e.g., incorporated on 15 October, due by 14 December annually)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Notice of default issued by the Director; continued non-filing for at least one additional annual cycle can result in administrative dissolution under s.212(1) CBCA, terminating corporate capacity until revival is obtained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; any balance of tax due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for eligible Canadian-controlled private corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; a minimum CAD 100 penalty may be charged for any late-filed T2 return; interest accrues on unpaid balances.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue-based threshold under the CBCA; an independent auditor must be appointed for distributing corporations. Non-distributing corporations may dispense with an audit if every shareholder consents via unanimous resolution or written consent for the fiscal year prior to the audit appointment deadline.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is required for publicly accountable or distributing corporations; private non-distributing corporations may elect to apply Canadian ASPE (GAAP) or IFRS consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO filing is submitted to Corporations Canada. The CBCA requires maintenance of a Register of Individuals with Significant Control, updated within 15 days of any change in significant control; management must verify the register annually at the AGM/board cycle and record any share transfers to ensure current data.
